# Windows 95 Web Designer — authentic Win95 design system extrapolated to modern web apps

Curated by Skill Harbor — @curiositech's windows-95-web-designer skill, listed here with credit to its creator: a complete design system for building modern web applications with an authentic Windows 95 aesthetic — not a recreation of 1995, but an extrapolation of Win95 into 2026. It ships a full CSS design system (the exact teal/gray/title-blue palette as CSS variables, the signature dark-to-light-blue title bar gradient, three-button window controls with 3D bevel box-shadows, Tahoma/MS Sans Serif typography) plus modern extrapolations: AI chatbots as Clippy descendants (character avatar, wizard dialogs, radio choices, "Tip of the Day"), mobile as the pocket-PC paradigm (Start button navigation, taskbar with open apps, icon-grid desktops), responsive breakpoints as multi-monitor metaphors, and Windows 95 Plus! themes for dark mode. It includes component patterns (Start menu, taskbar, dialog boxes for AI), anti-patterns (no hamburger menus, no FABs, no card layouts, no soft shadows — hard pixel shadows only), and a quick decision tree. Honest caveats: purely aesthetic — a novelty/retro treatment, not a design system for a serious product without heavy adaptation; assumes familiarity with modern CSS. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
